page: Amazon Web Services c9g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture. It provides 8 dedicated physical cores clocked at 3.3 GHz with 1 thread per core, backed by 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 16.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 compute-optimized memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server carries no local storage, requiring network-attached storage via Amazon EBS, includes no GPU accelerators, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data demonstrates exceptionally strong single-threaded performance from the Neoverse-V3 core design. Geekbench single-core testing reached 2,375.0 points (top 10%), text processing scored 3,141.0 points (top 10%), and single-threaded bzip3 decompression delivered 17.08 GB/sec (top 10%). PassMark memory performance also ranked in the top 10% with a score of 3,725.39. Multi-threaded metrics reflect balanced mid-tier compute throughput, evidenced by a multi-core Geekbench score of 13,369.0, stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 16,027.04, and software compilation via Clang scoring 21,265.0.

Performance tradeoffs emerge under specific computational patterns. Cryptographic and vector extension workloads show limitations, with the PassMark CPU encryption test posting 2,357.92 points (bottom 25%) and 7B model LLM prompt processing ranking in the bottom 25% at 22.5 tokens/sec. Conversely, lightweight token generation remains robust, achieving 298.71 tokens/sec on small 135M models. Lacking hardware GPUs and local NVMe storage, throughput is governed by EBS bandwidth and core capacity.

Qualitatively, the c9g.2xlarge delivers efficient single-thread and memory throughput per vCPU without the hyperthreading overhead found on shared-thread systems. The instance is suited for batch processing, CI/CD code compilation pipelines, data compression tasks, web serving clusters, and containerized microservices requiring dedicated physical ARM cores.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.2xlarge is an ARM-based compute-optimized instance powered by AWS Neoverse-V3 processors on the Nitro System. It is configured with 8 dedicated physical vCPUs at 3.3 GHz, 16.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core), 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and no bundled local storage or GPUs. The architecture shows top-tier single-core execution speed, ranking in the top 10% in Geekbench single-core, text processing, and PassMark memory benchmarks. Multi-threaded processing and static web serving deliver reliable mid-tier throughput, though performance dips on cryptographic benchmarks and larger language model prompt processing. This configuration offers balanced efficiency for dedicated ARM execution environments, making it suitable for CI/CD compilation, data compression pipelines, microservices, and web application serving.
